description: For claims with no payments (not p), the merge leaves indemnity_amt, expense_amt and recovery_amt missing. The not-p block (lines 96-101) only resets n_payments, n_recoveries, total_paid and recovery_flag. gross_paid uses '+' on missing values and net_paid is sum() of only missing values, so both come out missing instead of 0.

impact.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, CAST(0 AS DOUBLE) AS amount_affected FROM golden_dw_claims_enriched WHERE has_payment = 0 AND (indemnity_amt IS NULL OR expense_amt IS NULL OR recovery_amt IS NULL OR gross_paid IS NULL OR net_paid IS NULL)

impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, CAST(0 AS DOUBLE) AS amount_affected FROM golden_dw_claims_enriched WHERE has_payment = 0 AND (indemnity_amt IS NULL OR expense_amt IS NULL OR recovery_amt IS NULL OR gross_paid IS NULL OR net_paid IS NULL)
intended_behaviour: CR-1873 keeps unpaid claims with explicit zeros. indemnity_amt, expense_amt and recovery_amt should be set to 0 in the not-p block, so that gross_paid and net_paid are 0.
title: Split amounts, gross_paid and net_paid left missing for claims with no payments

description: total_paid uses the sum statement, which ignores missing values. The type split uses 'indemnity_amt = indemnity_amt + amount' (and the same for expense and recovery). One missing amount therefore makes that bucket missing, and it stays missing for every later payment on the claim. gross_paid and net_paid are then wrong as well.

impact.query: WITH p AS (SELECT cp.claim_id, upper(trim(cp.payment_type)) AS pt, cp.amount FROM stg_claim_payments cp WHERE (cp.payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' OR cp.payment_date IS NULL) AND cp.claim_id IN (SELECT claim_id FROM stg_claims)), b AS (SELECT claim_id, pt, SUM(amount) AS s, MAX(CASE WHEN amount IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_null FROM p WHERE pt IN ('INDEMNITY','EXPENSE','RECOVERY') GROUP BY claim_id, pt) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT claim_id) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(COALESCE(s,0))),0) AS amount_affected FROM b WHERE has_null = 1

impact_query: WITH p AS (SELECT cp.claim_id, upper(trim(cp.payment_type)) AS pt, cp.amount FROM stg_claim_payments cp WHERE (cp.payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' OR cp.payment_date IS NULL) AND cp.claim_id IN (SELECT claim_id FROM stg_claims)), b AS (SELECT claim_id, pt, SUM(amount) AS s, MAX(CASE WHEN amount IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_null FROM p WHERE pt IN ('INDEMNITY','EXPENSE','RECOVERY') GROUP BY claim_id, pt) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT claim_id) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(COALESCE(s,0))),0) AS amount_affected FROM b WHERE has_null = 1
intended_behaviour: Add up the split the same way as total_paid, ignoring missing amounts (sum statement or sum()), so the bucket holds the sum of the amounts that are known.
title: A missing payment amount wipes out the payment-type bucket for the rest of the claim

description: Payments are sorted by claim_id and _row_seq (the order they were keyed). first_payment_date is the date on the first keyed row and last_payment_date is the date on the last keyed row. If payments were keyed out of date order, these are not the earliest and latest payment dates.

impact.query: WITH m AS (SELECT claim_id, MIN(payment_date) AS mn, MAX(payment_date) AS mx, SUM(CASE WHEN payment_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_null FROM stg_claim_payments WHERE payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' OR payment_date IS NULL GROUP BY claim_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_dw_claims_enriched g JOIN m ON g.claim_id = m.claim_id WHERE m.n_null = 0 AND (NOT (g.first_payment_date <=> m.mn) OR NOT (g.last_payment_date <=> m.mx))

impact_query: WITH m AS (SELECT claim_id, MIN(payment_date) AS mn, MAX(payment_date) AS mx, SUM(CASE WHEN payment_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_null FROM stg_claim_payments WHERE payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' OR payment_date IS NULL GROUP BY claim_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_dw_claims_enriched g JOIN m ON g.claim_id = m.claim_id WHERE m.n_null = 0 AND (NOT (g.first_payment_date <=> m.mn) OR NOT (g.last_payment_date <=> m.mx))
intended_behaviour: first_payment_date = min(payment_date) and last_payment_date = max(payment_date) over the claim's payments up to the reporting date.
title: First and last payment dates taken from keying order, not from the dates

description: In SAS a missing date is lower than any value, so where=(payment_date <= &as_of) keeps payments with no date. Undated payments are counted in n_payments and total_paid, and the type split, and can make first_payment_date or last_payment_date missing.

impact.query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cp.claim_id) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(cp.amount)),0) AS amount_affected FROM stg_claim_payments cp WHERE cp.payment_date IS NULL AND cp.claim_id IN (SELECT claim_id FROM golden_dw_claims_enriched)

impact_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cp.claim_id) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(cp.amount)),0) AS amount_affected FROM stg_claim_payments cp WHERE cp.payment_date IS NULL AND cp.claim_id IN (SELECT claim_id FROM golden_dw_claims_enriched)
intended_behaviour: Keep only payments with a known date on or before the reporting date (INC-1677): add 'and not missing(payment_date)'.
title: Payments with a missing payment_date get past the reporting-date filter

description: recovery_amt is built from payment_type = 'RECOVERY', but n_recoveries and recovery_flag count every negative amount. Negative indemnity or expense corrections (reversals) are therefore counted and flagged as recoveries, and any RECOVERY row keyed with a positive amount is missed.

impact.query: WITH p AS (SELECT claim_id, upper(trim(payment_type)) AS pt, amount FROM stg_claim_payments WHERE payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' OR payment_date IS NULL), c AS (SELECT claim_id, SUM(CASE WHEN amount < 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_neg, SUM(CASE WHEN pt = 'RECOVERY' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_rec FROM p GROUP BY claim_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_dw_claims_enriched g JOIN c ON g.claim_id = c.claim_id WHERE c.n_neg <> c.n_rec

impact_query: WITH p AS (SELECT claim_id, upper(trim(payment_type)) AS pt, amount FROM stg_claim_payments WHERE payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' OR payment_date IS NULL), c AS (SELECT claim_id, SUM(CASE WHEN amount < 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_neg, SUM(CASE WHEN pt = 'RECOVERY' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_rec FROM p GROUP BY claim_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_dw_claims_enriched g JOIN c ON g.claim_id = c.claim_id WHERE c.n_neg <> c.n_rec
intended_behaviour: Identify a recovery the same way recovery_amt does, i.e. payment_type = 'RECOVERY', so that n_recoveries, recovery_flag and recovery_amt agree.
title: Recoveries identified by a negative amount, not by payment_type

description: total_paid includes every payment. The split only recognises INDEMNITY, EXPENSE and RECOVERY. Payments with any other or missing payment_type are left out of indemnity_amt, expense_amt and recovery_amt, so gross_paid and net_paid do not add up to total_paid.

impact.query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cp.claim_id) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(cp.amount)),0) AS amount_affected FROM stg_claim_payments cp WHERE (cp.payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' OR cp.payment_date IS NULL) AND (cp.payment_type IS NULL OR upper(trim(cp.payment_type)) NOT IN ('INDEMNITY','EXPENSE','RECOVERY')) AND cp.claim_id IN (SELECT claim_id FROM golden_dw_claims_enriched)

impact_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cp.claim_id) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(cp.amount)),0) AS amount_affected FROM stg_claim_payments cp WHERE (cp.payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' OR cp.payment_date IS NULL) AND (cp.payment_type IS NULL OR upper(trim(cp.payment_type)) NOT IN ('INDEMNITY','EXPENSE','RECOVERY')) AND cp.claim_id IN (SELECT claim_id FROM golden_dw_claims_enriched)
intended_behaviour: Every payment should go to a bucket (or an 'other' bucket) so that net_paid matches total_paid, or such types should be rejected explicitly.
title: Payment types outside the three known values are dropped from the split and from gross/net paid

description: stg.claims is sorted without NODUPKEY, so any claim_id that appears more than once on the register comes out more than once, each copy carrying the same payment totals. risk_scoring.sas then counts that claim's paid amounts more than once.

impact.query: WITH d AS (SELECT claim_id, COUNT(*) AS c, MAX(total_paid) AS tp FROM golden_dw_claims_enriched GROUP BY claim_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) SELECT COALESCE(SUM(c - 1),0) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM((c - 1) * ABS(tp)),0) AS amount_affected FROM d

impact_query: WITH d AS (SELECT claim_id, COUNT(*) AS c, MAX(total_paid) AS tp FROM golden_dw_claims_enriched GROUP BY claim_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) SELECT COALESCE(SUM(c - 1),0) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM((c - 1) * ABS(tp)),0) AS amount_affected FROM d
intended_behaviour: One row per claim: deduplicate the register (for example keep the latest _row_seq per claim_id) before the merge.
title: Duplicate claim_id on the register produces repeated output rows
